Regulation: B.C. Reg. 137/2026
Made under: Workers Compensation Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 20, 2026

B.C. Reg. 137/2026, deposited July 20, 2026, under theWORKERS COMPENSATION ACT[sections 110, 111 and 117]. Resolution of the Workers’ Compensation Board, dated July 16, 2026. The Workers’ Compensation Board orders that, effective September 1, 2027, the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97, is amended as set out in the attached Appendix. — W. L. CRONK,Chair, Board of Directors. 1	Section 4.9 of the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97, is amended (a)	in subsection (1) by striking out "a machine or piece of equipment to have an inspection and maintenance record" and substituting "that there be inspection and maintenance records for a machine or piece of equipment", (b)	in subsection (2) by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (b), by adding ", and" at the end of paragraph (c) and by adding the following paragraph: (d)	contain an entry for each certification carried out under section 4.12.3[periodic certification as safe for use]for the equipment., and (c)	by repealing subsection (3) and substituting the following: (3)	If this Regulation requires that there be inspection and maintenance records for a machine or piece of equipment, then detailed reports of inspections, maintenance, repairs and modifications, as applicable, and the certificates issued under section 4.12.3 (2) (b), must be (a)	kept for the duration of the service life of the machine or equipment, and (b)	reasonably available at the workplace and made available on request to the operator and to anyone else involved in the operation, inspection, testing or maintenance of the machine or equipment. 2	Part 4 is amended by adding the following heading after section 4.12: Periodic Certification as Safe for Use. 3	The following sections are added after the heading "Periodic Certification as Safe for Use": 4.12.1(1)	In this section and sections 4.12.2 to 4.12.4: "documentation"has the meaning given to it in subsections (2) and (3); "misadventure"has the same meaning as in section 14.16.1[certification following misadventure]; "reposition"has the same meaning as in section 14.73.1[definitions]; "tower crane"has the same meaning as in section 14.73.1; (2)	The documentation for equipment consists of the following documents:

minutes_briefs.title: BC employers must keep machine records for life and get periodic safety certification starting September 2027
minutes_briefs.summary: BC Regulation 137/2026 changes the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation (the rules for workplace safety in BC). Starting September 1, 2027, employers must keep detailed inspection, maintenance, repair and modification records for machines and equipment for the whole time the equipment is used. These records must be available at the workplace when an operator or anyone doing inspection, testing or maintenance asks for them. The regulation also adds a new 'periodic certification as safe for use' process, which requires equipment to be certified safe on a set schedule, and those certificates must be kept in the records too.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Review your machine and equipment record-keeping now and set up a system to keep inspection, maintenance and certification records for the full service life of each machine, available at the workplace.

key_dates.label: BC machine record-keeping and periodic certification rules take effect

minutes_briefs.industries: Construction & Development, Natural Resources, Transportation & Logistics
